findings.claim: In the Edexcel 1ET0 Section B exam, context is assessed through AO3
findings.truth: "Edexcel 1ET0" is a banned spec code in lesson fields; the house validator rejects the whole unit on it. Reworded to "the post-1914 novel essay".

findings.claim: <dfn ... data-def="A story or narrative that uses symbolic characters and events to convey a deeper moral or philosophical meaning.">original sin</dfn>
findings.truth: The glossary pop-up on "original sin" carried the definition of "allegory". The lesson's own glossary and its other "original sin" dfn give the correct Christian-doctrine definition.
findings.evidence: L01 glossary_terms entry "original sin"; identical dfn in the same lesson at n13

findings.claim: Question 1 ladder: "Top band (33-40) ... Top band (25-32) ... Upper-mid band (17-24) ... Lower-mid band (9-16) ... Lower band (1-8)"
findings.truth: Two bands were both labelled "Top band" and the mid band was missing, so a 25-32 answer was marked top band. Relabelled 25-32 Upper-mid and 17-24 Mid, matching the other 47 questions in the unit.
findings.evidence: ladder audit of all 48 practice questions in the unit; only this one is malformed

findings.claim: <dfn ... data-def="A long, heavy knife used for cutting through thick vegetation, used by Jack to hunt pigs on the island.">signal fire</dfn>
findings.truth: The glossary pop-up on "signal fire" carried the definition of a machete. Replaced with the lesson's own glossary definition of the signal fire.

findings.claim: <dfn ... data-def="A scene in which one character speaks at length to the audience or to themselves...">encounter</dfn>
findings.truth: The glossary pop-up on "encounter" carried the definition of a soliloquy. Replaced with the lesson's own glossary definition of "encounter".

findings.claim: the boys "wedded to her in lust," and Roger drives his spear "right up her ass."
findings.truth: Roger drives the spear but says nothing. The phrase is Robert's, shouted as a joke after the kill: "Robert stabilized the thing in a phrase which was received uproariously. 'Right up her ass!'"
findings.evidence: Lord of the Flies ch. 8 (archive.org full text, item lord-of-the-flies-william-golding, lines 7245-7252)

findings.claim: By the end of the chapter, Jack has established his own tribe at Castle Rock, with himself as chief
findings.truth: In ch. 8 Jack's group camps at the far end of the island and Jack only says "Now listen. We might go later to the castle rock." The tribe is established at Castle Rock by ch. 10. "at Castle Rock" removed.
findings.evidence: ch. 8: "We might go later to the castle rock"; ch. 10: "When Roger came to the neck of land that joined the Castle Rock to the mainland"

findings.claim: bioluminescent creatures that form a "bright, moving light" around him (repeated in flashcard 13)
findings.truth: "bright, moving light" is not in the novel. Ch. 9 reads: "the creatures made a moving patch of light as they gathered at the edge".

findings.claim: "His mind was crowded with memories" - Ralph now carries the weight of everything he has witnessed and done. (also practice question 6 stimulus, and the memorise-this list in lesson 8)
findings.truth: The line is Jack's, in chapter 4, immediately after the first pig kill: "His mind was crowded with memories; memories of the knowledge that had come to them when they closed in on the struggling pig". It is not Ralph and not the ending. The false quotation removed from the prose; the practice-question stimulus replaced with a verified line about Ralph ("There was a stillness about Ralph as he sat that marked him out", ch. 1).
findings.evidence: ch. 4, full text line 3525; single occurrence in the novel

findings.claim: "...not as a favour. I ask you because what's right is right."
findings.truth: The closing clause is invented. Ch. 11 reads: "I don't ask you to be a sport, I'll say, not because you're strong, but because what's right's right." The opening also dropped "in my hands". Both restored.

findings.claim: By the end, Roger is described as an "executioner" (and flashcard 12: "Which title is Roger given by the end of the novel?" / "Executioner.")
findings.truth: The word "executioner" appears nowhere in the novel. Ch. 11 reads: "The hangman's horror clung round him." A memorised quotation that does not exist in the text was being taught. Prose and flashcard both corrected to the real line.
findings.evidence: full-text search: 0 hits for "executioner"; ch. 11 line 9867 "The hangman's horror clung round him"

findings.claim: Golding, who witnessed the aftermath of the Holocaust, understood that the most dangerous people are not charismatic leaders...
findings.truth: Golding served in the Royal Navy: the Bismarck pursuit, D-Day (commanding a rocket-firing landing craft) and Walcheren. He did not witness the Holocaust or its aftermath. Reworded to "writing after the Holocaust came to light".

findings.claim: analysing Golding's symbolism allows you to write about language, form and structure (AO1) while connecting to context (AO3)
findings.truth: Language, form and structure is AO2, not AO1 - and AO2 is not assessed at all on the post-1914 novel question, which is AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8. Students were being pointed at an objective that earns nothing here, under the wrong code.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md: "Section B - Post-1914 British play or novel... Assessment Objectives covered are AO1, AO3 and AO4"

findings.claim: AO4 (SPaG) rewards accurate spelling, punctuation and the use of literary terminology like 'symbolism', 'foreshadowing', 'allegory' and 'microcosm'.
findings.truth: AO4 is "use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation". Subject terminology belongs to AO2, which is not assessed on this question. The tip told students to chase 8 marks with the wrong technique.

findings.claim: For exam success: ... and use literary terminology throughout for AO4.
findings.truth: Same AO4 error, in the takeaway list a student revises from. Replaced with accurate spelling and punctuation for the technical marks.

findings.claim: Key Quotations to Memorise list: "His mind was crowded with memories" - Ralph's self-knowledge at the end.
findings.truth: Jack's line from chapter 4 (see F9), sitting in a closed-book memorisation list under Ralph's name. Replaced with "The mask compelled them" (ch. 4, verified), which covers face paint and group violence - a theme the list otherwise omits.

findings.claim: "Which AO carries the most weight in Edexcel's modern text essay?" / "AO1 - informed personal response with quotations."
findings.truth: AO1 and AO3 are equal on this question at 16 marks each, with 8 for AO4. The question as written has no correct answer. Recast as the mark split.
findings.evidence: Edexcel 1ET0 Paper 1 Section B: 40 marks = AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8

findings.claim: The conch (democracy) is established in Chapter 1, challenged in Chapter 4, ignored by Chapter 8, and destroyed in Chapter 11.
findings.truth: Jack's first challenge - "The conch doesn't count on top of the mountain" - is chapter 2, as lessons 2 and 7 both say. Changed to Chapter 2.

findings.claim: reduced by simile to "a pig after it has been killed" (also flashcard 10, and the mark scheme of lesson 5 question 4)
findings.truth: The novel reads "Piggy's arms and legs twitched a bit, like a pig's after it has been killed" - possessive. Lesson 5 quotes it correctly in prose. Not mark-affecting; recorded rather than edited.

findings.claim: "Simon is presented as a _____ figure who confronts evil, discovers truth, and is killed by those he tries to save." Keyed answer "Christ-like"; distractor "prophetic".
findings.truth: The keyed answer is right, but the lesson's own sentence reads "a prophetic or Christ-like figure", so a student who picks the distractor is marked wrong for the lesson's own wording. Question quality, not a fact error.

findings.claim: rejected by 21 publishers before Faber and Faber accepted it in 1954 (also flashcard 4)
findings.truth: Sources disagree. Wikipedia's Golding article says seven publishers; the Lord of the Flies article says only "many publishers". 21 is widely repeated but not securely sourced. Never mark-affecting in an essay, so left alone.

findings.claim: Every practice question in the unit ends its ladder "Lower band (1-8)".
findings.truth: The house ladder name is "Low band". All 48 questions use "Lower band", so it is consistent within the unit and not a banned string. Renaming all 48 was judged churn, not a fix.

findings.claim: For a modern-text essay, you will typically be assessed on AO1 ..., AO3 (context) and sometimes AO4 ... Check your exam board's specimen paper for the exact format and mark weightings.
findings.truth: Board-generic hedging in a board-specific lesson. On this board AO4 is always assessed and worth 8 of the 40. Not wrong, but weaker than the same lesson's knowledge check, which states the split correctly.

summary: 8 lessons checked against the Edexcel 1ET0 spec and the full text of the novel (archive.org item lord-of-the-flies-william-golding). 23 findings: 6 HIGH, 10 MEDIUM, 7 LOW; 18 fixed in 23 surgical edits, 5 recorded as notes. The two systemic faults are an AO4 misconception (AO4 taught as literary terminology rather than technical accuracy, in the exam tip and the takeaways of lesson 8, plus AO2 content labelled AO1 in lesson 7) and three fabricated or misattributed quotations that had reached memorisation lists and a practice stimulus - Jack's "His mind was crowded with memories" sold as Ralph's ending, Roger's non-existent "executioner", and an invented clause in Piggy's conch speech. Three glossary pop-ups also carried the definition of an entirely different term.
